title: Smoke run: one bug-fix rule on Haiku at effort low and medium
question: Does the one-sentence bug-fixing rule, delivered only as the work dir CLAUDE.md, change the pass rate of Haiku at effort low and at effort medium on fx3 and fx4b?

verdict.label: descriptive
verdict.text: smoke run without preregistration, 3 trials per cell, no claim: pooled rule 2/6 against none 1/6 at effort low, rule 4/6 against none 1/6 at effort medium

notes: The run tested the steps of evals/CONTRIBUTING.md with a small budget: 2 configurations, 2 fixtures, 2 arms, 3 trials per cell, 24 trials, 0.20 USD in total.

It used the runner and the isolation of 2026-11-11-rule-bug-fix-callers-matrix, with Haiku added to the Claude model table and the configurations set to claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low and medium. The rule text, prompts, graders, tool allowlist, 20 max turns and 300 s timeout are unchanged.

No preregistration was written, so the analyzer's per-configuration decision lines are not verdicts. The analyzer prints rule helps for effort medium (rule minus none +0.50, CI [+0.17, +0.83]). That label applies the matrix rule to a run that did not preregister it, so it is exploratory.
The canary isolation check was not repeated. The runner's isolation flags are the ones that the matrix probes checked on Claude Code 2.1.322. This run used Claude Code 2.1.332.
Claude Code does not echo the effort in its init event, so effort is the flag passed. The init event echoed the model claude-haiku-5-5 in all 24 trials.
Exposure by first-turn input tokens: rule exposed 6 of 6 and none clean 6 of 6 per configuration. No trial timed out, leaked the grader or saw another trial's work dir. No infra failure, no retry.
The fixture hashes equal the recorded fx3 and fx4b values, recomputed from the fixture trees on 2026-11-28. The runner checked the grader hashes before grading.
Duration and tokens come from the result event of each trial.
